subject: Re: Next steps — SDK smokekit, auth & embedding/reranker onramp
messages:
From: Sam Richards <sam.richards@luminahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Amina Rahman <amina@luminahealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: SDK quickstart & local testing requirements

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion. Amina and I pulled together a short list of what we need to feel comfortable running a small pilot (3–4 week) with Redwood: 

- A simple SDK quickstart (Python + TypeScript) we can run locally (no cloud creds) that demonstrates: auth flow (OIDC + API key fallback), routing to a hosted model vs. a dedicated endpoint, and structured tool-calling output.
- An example that shows embeddings + reranker flow end-to-end: ingest -> embed -> store -> rerank (we're using Postgres for storage) with minimal glue code.
- Clear instructions for sandbox env setup: Node 18 / Python 3.11, recommended virtualenv/npm scripts, required env vars, and a sample .env.example.
- Recommended test cases / smoke tests we can run (latency checks, shaped prompts to validate structured output, and sample prompts for reranking quality checks).

I've attached a quick requirements spreadsheet (Lumi-reqs.xlsx) that lists our high-level compliance constraints (data residency and logging) and a preference for OIDC integration with our Okta tenant. Can you confirm whether the local quickstart can run without opening inbound ports and whether the SDK will provide a local mock mode for tool-calling and embeddings?

Best,
Sam
Director of ML Integrations
Lumina Health

---
Attachment: Lumi-reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sam Richards <sam.richards@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Amina Rahman <amina@luminahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T10:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SDK quickstart & local testing requirements

Sam — thanks for the clear list and the spreadsheet. High level recap + our plan below (short and actionable).

Recap of asks you called out:
- Local SDK quickstart: Python + TypeScript, no inbound ports required, supports both API key and OIDC (Okta) for auth.
- Demonstration of routing: show a call to hosted Redwood API and a call to a Dedicated endpoint (we'll simulate Dedicated via a pinned model variant in the quickstart).
- Structured output / tool-calling: quick example that emits a JSON-safe schema and a separate local "tool" runner that accepts the structured response.
- Embeddings + reranker: small pipeline using our embed endpoint -> store into Postgres -> run a simple cosine similarity and Redwood reranker to re-score top-K.
- Environment & smoke tests: Node 18, Python 3.11, .env.example, npm/python scripts to run unit smoke checks (latency/format validation).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and timing:
1) Today — we’ll send: Redwood SDK quickstart draft (redwood-sdk-quickstart.md) + repo checklist and Drive folder with sample apps.
2) By Thu (48h) — delivery: Python quickstart repo + TS quickstart repo (each README with env setup + scripts).
3) Next Tue — 30-minute screening session (live share) to run through local smoke tests together.
4) Week after — Pilot kickoff: we’ll hand over a small sample dataset and assist with Okta OIDC config and routing policy.

Action items (owners):
- Redwood: provide quickstart repos, smokekit, and a small demo script to simulate Dedicated routing (Jonas / Karthik).
- Lumina: confirm preferred local test machine (macOS vs. Ubuntu) and Okta test tenant details (Sam / Amina).

Notes on the local mock mode: the SDK includes a "--offline-mock" flag that returns deterministic structured-call responses and fake embeddings for local unit testing; you won't need to open inbound ports for the quickstart. We'll include a sample Postgres docker-compose for local storage and scripts to seed a tiny dataset.

I'll attach the draft quickstart and a short checklist; Karthik and Marissa looped for implementation details. If that plan looks good, confirm the Tue screening window that works for you and we'll lock time.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

---
Attachment: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (stub, 8KB)
Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xQ-lumina-onramp
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T11:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SDK quickstart & local testing requirements (implementation notes)

Quick tech notes for the repo and smokekit — copying into the quickstart doc as well: 

1) Local stack (docker-compose):
   - Postgres 15 (local port 5433), admin user redwood_test, sample DB redwood_dev
   - Local "reranker" process: small Python service that calls /embeddings -> upserts vectors -> runs top-K then calls /rerank endpoint with candidate set.

2) Auth flows to include:
   - API_KEY: env REDWOOD_API_KEY; simple.
   - OIDC (Okta): we will provide an example redirect-less flow using client credentials + a sample Okta test tenant config (no inbound callback required for the quickstart). Add a note: if customer requires user-bound tokens, we can demo authorization code flow in a follow-up.

3) SDK features to highlight in examples:
   - Streaming vs. chunked responses (show at least one streaming example for structured output).
   - tool_calling sample: the mock tool runner accepts a JSON schema, validates shape, and returns deterministic output.
   - embeddings: use deterministic hash-based vectors for offline-mock (--offline-mock) so reranker reproducibility is high during smoke tests.

4) Test cases (smoke):
   - smoke/01-env-check: verifies Node/Python versions and env vars.
   - smoke/02-auth: exercise API_KEY and OIDC client-credentials to get token and call /models.
   - smoke/03-structured-output: run a generation that returns the JSON schema and validate keys/types.
   - smoke/04-rerank-pipeline: ingest 10 small documents, run embeddings, run reranker, assert top1 matches expected hash.

5) Readme + .env.example keys: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL, OKTA_DOMAIN, OKTA_CLIENT_ID, OKTA_CLIENT_SECRET, DATABASE_URL.

I also suggest a small TypeScript sample called "ts-smokekit-search" and a Python counterpart "py-smokekit-search" to keep parity. I'll push a starter branch by end of day to the shared Drive folder.

—Karthik
Senior Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the MAP. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Local machine: we’ll standardize on Ubuntu 22.04 for the dev sandbox.
- Okta test tenant: we can provision a service account for client_credentials; I will send the tenant ID and a temporary client secret via our secure channel later today.
- Data residency & logs: we can tolerate that the quickstart uses Redwood hosted endpoints for the demo so long as logs are not persisted beyond 7 days — please confirm this in writing.

We'd like the screening session on Tue at 10:00 AM PT. Can you please confirm Karthik/Marissa availability and whether the smokekit will include the docker-compose for Postgres? Also — will the offline-mock vectors be deterministic across runs for CI assertions?

Thanks,
Sam

- Screening session: Tue 10:00 AM PT (Jonas/Karthik/Marissa confirmed). I’ll send a calendar invite with a link to the Drive folder and a short meeting agenda (run smoke tests, validate OIDC flow, demo reranker).

Action items (final):
- Redwood (Jonas/Karthik): push initial quickstart repos + sample-apps-checklist.zip to Drive by EOD today.
